how: Drop-in salsa and bachata classes with socials run at Latin dance studios across Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx.
Chhandayan Center for Indian Music in Midtown Manhattan lists group sitar and tabla classes.
Beginner stand-up courses of about six weeks end in a graduation show at a Manhattan comedy club.
Lindy hop series for beginners run at the 92nd Street Y and Chelsea studios, with no partner needed.
Chhandayan runs small-group tabla classes (10 students or fewer) for all ages and levels with an annual recital.
Soh Daiko, founded 1979 at the New York Buddhist Church, runs public taiko workshops and recruits members; Taikoza offers paid classes.
Beginner and adult tap classes are widely offered at Manhattan dance studios.
Chinese (Peking) opera is performed by local societies such as the New York Chinese Opera Society and Yeh Yu; regular public classes are not clearly listed.
Textile Arts Center in Brooklyn lists a batik one-day intensive on its workshop calendar.
Textile Arts Center in Brooklyn lists embroidery and bead embroidery workshops.
Manhattan Graphics Center has practitioners in intaglio (including etching), relief, lithography and screenprint and runs classes.
Manhattan Graphics Center teaches lithography alongside intaglio, relief and screenprinting.
Manhattan Graphics Center offers screenprinting among its printmaking classes.
International Center of Photography runs courses through Open Education and has darkrooms and media labs; film and alternative processes are taught.
New York Film Academy offers filmmaking programmes and short-term workshops of 1 to 15 weeks.
UrbanGlass in Brooklyn runs Intro to Glassblowing and Glassblowing 101 classes for beginners.
UrbanGlass lists Flameworking and Beadmaking classes such as Hot Torch Basics Bootcamp for beginners.
NYC Resistor's shared space in downtown Brooklyn lists a laser cutter for members.
NYC Resistor hosts electronics classes (e.g. KiCad circuit board design) and members' maker projects.
OrigamiUSA runs monthly Folding Sundays meetings and special sessions at the American Museum of Natural History.
Fat Cat Fab Lab, a volunteer-run makerspace in the West Village, offers 3D printing and a 3D Printing 101 class.
Fat Cat Fab Lab has CNC routing with a members-only CNC safety class.
The Art Students League of New York offers painting classes at all levels on West 57th Street.

NYC Beekeeping, a volunteer group, runs a Saturday Series hands-on course, mentoring, newcomer events and community honey harvests.
New York Comic Con at the Javits Center holds cosplay competitions such as the Crown Championships of Cosplay.
Sandbox VR lists a New York City location for group VR gaming.
Sporcle Live runs pub trivia events with a Find a Game location finder; NYC bars host weekly quiz nights.
